title: DJ Turn Me Up
essence: A full house party in an Atlantis house: the DJ drops onto the decks and scratches, and the poet, standing at the bar as in the part 1 reading video, eyes shut and chin pressed down under the weight of his words, tells the love story while a projection wall behind him shows it: ghosts walking out of a dying vineyard, two wedding bands drifting apart, a house trucked off down one-way streets, eleven petals plucked off a daisy, three roads. The whole poem is one climb in volume: starved at the start, turnt up at the end, chin high, the room erupting.
palette_notes: Night interior #0b0f1e and the district cyan #01acd4 from Naraka Market (22ddf809 blue vapour, e3c427ae teal market crowd). Magenta #e0479e and amber #ffb04a from the neon container fronts (b631fc80, 79ea20ae) and the pink-orange haze of the crowd blur a883ad75. Haze violet #8a6fa8 is that same smoke. Vineyard green #6e8b3d fading to dry straw #c9b37a for the projected vineyard. Silver #cfd6e0 is the one accent, the silver lining in M6 (world module: level 8 spent exactly once).

full_text.line: DJ turn me up please. With eyes wide shut and my chin nested at the arc of the weight of these
spoken words, I have a story to tell. Of ghosts whispering unfolded delusions, birthed in purity
and dying and the veneers of sun-soaked evergreen fields are nourished. A love story of one by one
treasures escaping and devaluing themselves after defamed unsalted stars diminish their glares.
And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me
up. So I can speak of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a
shared home boxed in truck on separate one-way streets not built with u-turns or stop. Maybe
we shouldn't signs. A love story of years 11 years each plucked off as daisy pedals
we love we not. Of a future gone swiftly and a past left empty handed to pick a road of heavy rain
or a frontal fog or of dim night lights under a cloud with the silver lining. Of now turning
forth to face the lights and shadows one night at a time, one tear at a time. When called to a friend
at a time. One open mic at a time. Chin now nested high and volume turned up in a story to tell.

arc.beat: two wedding bands slide apart on a diagonal across a wounded sky; a house boxed into two trucks driving off down separate one-way streets

arc.beat: he holds a daisy to the mic and plucks eleven petals onto the bar; the guests mouth 'we love, we not'; a lighter goes up; the bare stem drops, his hand stays open

insights: Amplitude is the whole design: one envelope scales the poet, the mic and the central object of each movement, anchored at a fixed stage floor. In cut-out, print the poet's cards at two or three scales or scale the rig in comp.
Put the love story on the projection wall, not in the room: it keeps the poet at the bar (the treatment's source, Mark at the bar) and lets the images be flat prints, which cut-out does best.
Make the middle movements move: each has one quantity running the whole way (sky emptying, gap opening, petals counting down) and an arrival at the end; avoid holding still pictures for 14 s.
Reaction shots are the treatment's ask: give guests real faces and hands (hand on chest, lighter up, mouthing along).
The EX appears only as a projected ghost, back to us; this keeps the rule that his face is never seen.
Spend the silver accent only on the lining in M6.
future: The poet's chin-high pose and the open mic are the 'one open mic at a time' that leads into 08 (he leaves the party for the rooftop).
The house and its crowd are reused for the 14 'hot minute' ending and the vintage party echoes of 01.
The three-roads panel feeds 10's ride out of Atlantis.
The daisy is a small reusable prop for any later love-counting beat (13 How To Win My Heart).
